body:
Three diagnostic passes (sudo-queue/54, 55, 56) progressively ruled out every PJSIP-side possibility -- password correct, realm correct, digest math independently verified correct -- because the actual problem was one level up: this Asterisk install has both chan_sip (legacy) and chan_pjsip (modern) loaded, and chan_sip was grabbing the REGISTER for extension 1000 before PJSIP ever processed it, checking credentials against its own untouched stock sip.conf instead of pjsip_carepyre_phone.conf. Found via messages.log: 'chan_sip.c: Registration from <sip:1000@198.58.107.85> failed ... Wrong password'. sudo-queue/57 permanently disables chan_sip via modules.conf's noload directive. Session: sess-20260905-0712-8908a299

⚓ ☃
title: Real root cause of SIP 403 found: legacy chan_sip intercepting REGISTER, not a PJSIP/client bug
